title: Flat affine comparison and equivariance of the canonical open image
statement:
Let $R\to T$ be a ring homomorphism with flat spectrum morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V\to S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] that is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and whose every quasi-compact open is isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Let $E\subset |V|$ be an intersection of a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens, put $C=\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_V|_E)$, and let $W\subset V$ be any open subscheme contained in $E$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-a1-ringed-subspace, def-a1-intersection-structure-sections]. Write $j_E:E\to Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$ for the unique locally ringed space morphism inducing $\mathrm{id}_C$ on sections [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then $j_E|_W$ is an open immersion with image $J$. Set $V_T=V\times_S\operatorname{Spec}T$, $E_T=g^{-1}(E)$ and $W_T=g^{-1}(W)$ for the projection $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Identify $\Gamma(E_T,\mathcal O_{V_T}|_{E_T})=C\otimes_R T$ by $c\otimes t\mapsto g^\sharp(c)t$. The canonical map $j_{E_T}|_{W_T}$ equals the base change of $j_E|_W$ into $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_R T)$, and its image is exactly $J\times_S\operatorname{Spec}T$. More explicitly, for every affine open $L\subset W$, with $D=\Gamma(L,\mathcal O_L)$, the corresponding restriction map is $C\otimes_R T\to D\otimes_R T$, $c\otimes t\mapsto(c|_L)\otimes t$, and its square with $C\to D$ is a pushout of rings.
In particular let $T=A$, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ be also surjective, suppose $V\to S$ factors through $X$, and give $V\to X$ a descent datum $\varphi:V\times_S X\cong X\times_S V$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Suppose $E$ and $W$ are invariant under $\varphi$. Let $\psi:A\otimes_R C\to C\otimes_R A$ be the comorphism on the section rings of the inverse images of $E$, and set $\theta=\operatorname{Spec}\psi$. Under the preceding comparisons on the two sides, $\theta\circ(j_E|_W\times\mathrm{id}_X)=(\mathrm{id}_X\times j_E|_W)\circ\varphi|_{W\times_S X}$. Consequently $\theta(J\times_S X)=X\times_S J$ as open subschemes, and $W\cong J$ intertwines their restricted descent data.

proof.text: Construct the actual sheafed-space maps W to E and E_T to E by inverse-image adjunction, using [def-a1-ringed-subspace] and [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. The ambient inclusion of E is a monomorphism of sheafed spaces: its base is injective, and [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk] identifies its stalk maps with isomorphisms. The adjunction unit equations show that both ways of restricting the ambient scheme map agree after this monomorphism, hence agree. Applying global sections gives naturality of the restriction homomorphism. The unit equation also identifies restriction of the ambient structural ring map with the actual structural map on W. The Gamma-Spec adjunction translates these ring equations into naturality and the structural-map equation for the canonical open affinization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-intersection-canonical-affine-embedding] to $V,E,W$: the assumed quasi-affineness of every quasi-compact open is exactly its hypothesis. It gives the unique $j_E$, its restriction corresponding to $C\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, and the open immersion $h=j_E|_W$ with open image $J$. Apply [lem-a1-intersection-sections-flat-base-change] to $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $R\to T$, and the given nonempty family defining $E$. Quasi-separatedness and flatness are hypotheses here. Its canonical isomorphism $\alpha:C\otimes_RT\simeq\Gamma(E_T,\mathcal O|_{E_T})$ sends $c\otimes t$ to $g^\sharp(c)t$. By [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction], this isomorphism specifies the canonical $j_{E_T}:E_T\to\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_RT)$ (the identity-on-sections map after the indicated identification).

source.place: Tags 0API, lemma-sits-in-functions, and 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change, used in Tag 0APK

proof.text: The canonical map h:W to Spec C is over Spec R: naturality of the Gamma-Spec adjunction identifies its composite with the structural map with W inclusion followed by f. The tensor pushout over R identifies Spec(C tensor T) with the affine fibre product. Restrict the ambient pullback square to W. The two projections of the canonical map from W_T agree with this restricted square: the first follows by restriction naturality on C, the second by the scalar formula on T. Cancelling the affine tensor pullback square gives the asserted IsPullback square. Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_fst then identifies its range with the inverse image of the range of h; an extra open-immersion base-change lemma is not needed.

source.place: Tag 0APK final diagram; affine tensor-product and open base-change universal properties written out

proof.text: Both $\beta$ and $j_{E_T}|_{W_T}$ correspond to $C\otimes_RT\to\Gamma(W_T,\mathcal O_{W_T})$, $c\otimes t\mapsto(g^\sharp(c))|_{W_T}\,t$. For $\beta$ this follows from its two projections in Step 3; for the canonical map it follows by restricting the formula for $\alpha$ in Step 2. The restrictions here are those of the same sheaf comorphism, so pullback of $c$ followed by restriction is restriction followed by pullback. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](3) gives equality of the ring maps, and the bijection [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] gives equality of the morphisms. Thus the canonical restricted map has the asserted open image, without needing any quasi-compactness of $W$.

source.place: Tag 0APK final diagram: canonical maps compared on sections using Tag 01I1, lemma-morphism-into-affine

proof.text: Let $L\subset W$ be affine and set $D=\Gamma(L,\mathcal O_L)$. The same affine universal-property argument of Step 3 gives $L_T=\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_RT)$. The map of Step 4 on this chart is therefore $C\otimes_RT\to D\otimes_RT$, $c\otimes t\mapsto(c|_L)\otimes t$. Its square with $C\to D$ and the maps $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, $d\mapsto d\otimes1$ is a pushout: for compatible homomorphisms $u:D\to B$ and $v:C\otimes_RT\to B$, give $B$ its $R$-algebra structure through $u$. Put $w(t)=v(1\otimes t)$. Compatibility makes $w$ an $R$-algebra map. Clauses (2),(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give the unique map $D\otimes_RT\to B$, $d\otimes t\mapsto u(d)w(t)$; its composite with the top map is $v$, by equality on pure tensors. This proves the pushout claim for arbitrary commutative rings $B$.

source.place: Tag 0APK canonical flat affine pullback square, with the affine-chart ring pushout explicitly verified

proof.text: Now take $T=A$. Write $F_1=E\times_SX$, $F_2=X\times_SE$, and let $a:F_1\to\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_RA)$, $b:F_2\to\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RC)$ be the canonical maps. The left and right comparisons are the comparison of Step 2 and its factor-switched version. By definition of the comorphism in the statement, $\varphi_E^\sharp=\psi:A\otimes_RC\to C\otimes_RA$ in these coordinates. Both $b\circ\varphi_E$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)\circ a$ induce exactly this map on sections: $a$ and $b$ induce the identity in their section coordinates, and composition reverses comorphisms. Naturality and injectivity of [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] imply their equality. Restrict to the open $W\times_SX$; invariance gives its image under $\varphi$ as $X\times_SW$. Step 4 identifies the restricted $a,b$ with the two base changes of $h$, giving precisely the displayed equivariance equation. Since $\psi$ is an isomorphism, taking open images gives $\theta(J\times_SX)=X\times_SJ$, with their restricted structure sheaves [def-weil-open-immersion]. Finally $h:W\simeq J$ intertwines the restricted maps by this same equation. The cocycle identity of [def-pd-descent-datum] transfers under this isomorphism: substituting the conjugate of $\varphi$ in each of the three pullbacks cancels the adjacent $h^{-1}h$. Hence these are their restricted descent data. In Lean, obtain the two canonical section comparisons, psi and F from [lem-a1-invariant-intersection-affine-descent]. Naturality of restriction and the Gamma-Spec adjunction proves equivariance. The overlap is invertible by transport_transport and transport_self. For an arbitrary test-scheme point, factor its transported map through W using hWinv; cancel the tensor-swap and affine-pullback coordinate isomorphisms in F's overlap equation to identify its affine transport.

There are no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Source: Stacks 0APK (more-groupoids.tex, lemma-ind-quasi-affine). Its final diagram and the claim that the two inverse images of j(W) are equal come with no details; the item writes them out (D5/E5). The item's psi is the comorphism phi^# : A⊗C→C⊗A, the inverse of Stacks' psi, and theta = Spec psi has the correct direction. Step 2: the hypotheses of lem-a1-intersection-canonical-affine-embedding (every quasi-compact open quasi-affine) and of lem-a1-intersection-sections-flat-base-change (quasi-separated, flat, nonempty set-indexed family) are all assumed by the item. j_{E_T} is defined through the affine adjunction, not through the embedding lemma. Steps 3-4: the base change beta and the restricted canonical map have the same section map c⊗t↦g^#(c)|t, so they are equal by tensor uniqueness and adjunction injectivity; quasi-compactness of W is not needed. Step 5: I checked the chart pushout for arbitrary B by hand. Step 6: equivariance follows from adjunction injectivity, the images give theta(J×X)=X×J, and the cocycle transfers by conjugation along h. Edge cases checked: W or E empty, T=0, T=R, E=V affine. No duplicate: the sibling lem-a1-invariant-intersection-affine-descent covers psi and its cocycle, which is complementary. The declared tool_uses (inverse-image stalk, tensor universal property, open-immersion base change) are generic and I accept them. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding is a Mathlib leaf stating Stacks 01P9 (a quasi-affine scheme embeds openly into Spec of its global sections). That is general scheme theory, not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality or their proofs, so the citation is accepted. Advisory: Step 3 re-derives lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra and lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product, both existing leaves, from cited nodes; the argument is valid, so I made no change. No SGA source is cited.
